title: probabilistic-rule-serializer-and-constraint-bridge-for-streaming-toolcalls
author: Morgan Lee
description: Motivation: Streaming structured outputs and tool/function-calls can diverge when constraint backends (CFG grammar, regex, probabilistic samplers) disagree about partial-token state and escape sequences. This causes inconsistent framing for downstream tool callers and the OpenAI-compat layer, leading to truncated JSON or misrouted function calls. Goal: introduce a compact rule serializer and a probabilistic constraint bridge that aligns CFG/regex decisions with the tokenizer-aware streaming frontier, and add a small compat shim for OpenAI-style partial-token framing. Key changes: 1) Rule serializer: a compact, canonical on-wire format for grammar/regex constraints so the decoder and the streaming proxy can exchange constraint state efficiently; used for canary rollouts and replayability. 2) Probabilistic bridge: on token-edge ambiguity (subtoken splits, escaped delimiters) we compute a lightweight posterior over constraint accept/reject and use a deterministic tie-break policy to avoid flip-flopping mid-stream. This reduces streaming retractions for structured outputs. 3) Escape-sequence coordinator: normalizes model-provided escape sequences (backslashes, quotes, unicode escapes) into a canonical tokenized representation before constraint evaluation to avoid double-decoding. 4) OpenAI-compat shim: adds a tolerant framing mode that buffers the minimal number of bytes required to disambiguate toolcall boundaries while preserving early partial 'delta' streaming for latency-sensitive clients. 5) Tests & rollout: extensive unit tests for tokenizer-edgecases, newly added golden recordings for streaming canary, and a staged rollout plan with feature-flagged runtime toggles. Implementation notes: - The serializer is implemented as rule_serializer.{rs,py} (Rust core + Python bridge) and stores rule fingerprints and serialized predicate trees. - The probabilistic bridge lives in decoder/constraint_bridge.go and exposes a small API used by the streaming proxy. - The OpenAI compat shim is in openai_compat/stream_shim.ts and toggled via REDWOOD_OPENAI_COMPAT_STREAMING env. - Conservative performance opt: only compute the posterior when the tokenizer indicates a grapheme-split or when a rule fingerprint mismatch is detected. Compatibility and migration: - Backward compatible: old runtimes ignore unknown serializer versions and fall back to current CFG/regex backends. - Canary plan: enable serializer+bridge for 5% of production traffic, measure stream retraction rate and functioncall misfires for 72h, then 25% then full rollout. Testing: unit tests added for 42 tokenizer edgecases, integration tests with the example toolcall harness, and three new end-to-end recordings against the OpenAI-compat shim. Observability: new metrics: constraint.bridge.posterior_compute_count, streaming.retraction_rate, compat.shim.buffer_bytes_histogram. Migration checklist: - [x] Add serializer version header and compatibility guard - [x] Add posterior compute budget to runtime config - [x] Add feature flag + rollout plan - [x] Add golden streaming recordings - [x] Add e2e toolcall test harness run in CI Notes and follow-ups: we will follow up with a separate PR to expose the rule fingerprint format in the model catalog and add SDK helpers for users to pin serializer versions. Related: ENG-3421, ENG-3499, SUP-2101. Links: design doc https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3421/constraint-serializer-design (internal), test recordings stored in /bench/streaming/gold/serializer-bridge.
commits: feat(serializer): add canonical rule serializer and fingerprinting
feat(bridge): probabilistic constraint bridge and deterministic tie-break
fix(streaming): normalize escape sequences before constraint eval
feat(openai-compat): add streaming shim and env toggle
test: add tokenizer edgecase unit tests and golden recordings
ci: add canary job for serializer-bridge
review_comments: Aisha Kapoor: Nice approach. Two concerns: 1) computing a posterior per ambiguous token could be expensive under high throughput. Suggest adding a budget or sampling mechanism. 2) Need an explicit plan for serializer version skew during rolling restarts.

Morgan Lee: Addressed both. Added posterior_compute_budget config and fast-exit when tokenizer indicates non-ambiguous grapheme. Serializer carries a version header and runtimes ignore unknown versions to remain compatible.
Diego Martinez: Please add more unit tests around escaped unicode sequences (e.g. \u2028) and verify the shim doesn't change byte-level streaming for clients that rely on single-byte framing.

Morgan Lee: Added 12 unicode-specific edgecases and end-to-end recordings showing identical byte stream when shim operates in 'tolerant=false' mode. See tests in runtime/serializer and e2e recordings.
Yvonne Chen: CI flaked once in canary job, reran and passed. Approving for merge after small doc polish.
Morgan Lee: Polished docs and added clarifying note about SDK helpers planned for follow-up PR.
Release manager (informal): Please note release_notes mention when rolling out; this touches streaming and may require comms to integrators.
release_notes: Introduce rule serializer and probabilistic constraint bridge to reduce streaming retractions and toolcall misfires; add OpenAI-compat streaming shim; feature-flagged rollout and new observability metrics.
